text: Everything fails, all the time.

text: You build it, you run it.
author: Werner Vogels

text: Hope is not a strategy.

text: 100% is the wrong reliability target for basically everything.

text: SRE is what happens when you ask a software engineer to design an operations team.
author: Benjamin Treynor Sloss

text: If a human operator needs to touch your system during normal operations, you have a bug.

text: The cost of failure is education.

text: Complex systems run in degraded mode.

text: Safety is a characteristic of systems and not of their components.

text: Hindsight biases post-accident assessments of human performance.

text: Nines don't matter if users aren't happy.
author: Charity Majors

text: There is no compression algorithm for experience.

text: Premature optimization is the root of all evil.
author: Donald Knuth
source: Structured Programming with go to Statements, Computing Surveys (1974)

text: Beware of bugs in the above code; I have only proved it correct, not tried it.
author: Donald Knuth
source: Memo to Peter van Emde Boas (1977)

text: Science is what we understand well enough to explain to a computer. Art is everything else we do.
author: Donald Knuth

text: Simplicity is prerequisite for reliability.

source: EWD498, How do we tell truths that might hurt? (1975)

text: Program testing can be used to show the presence of bugs, but never to show their absence!

text: The competent programmer is fully aware of the strictly limited size of his own skull.

author: C. A. R. Hoare

text: The purpose of computing is insight, not numbers.
author: Richard Hamming
source: Numerical Methods for Scientists and Engineers (1962)

text: A distributed system is one in which the failure of a computer you didn't even know existed can render your own computer unusable.
author: Leslie Lamport
source: Email to a DEC SRC bulletin board (1987)

text: Everyone knows that debugging is twice as hard as writing a program in the first place.

source: The Elements of Programming Style, 2nd ed. (1978)

text: Controlling complexity is the essence of computer programming.
author: Brian Kernighan and P. J. Plauger

text: The most effective debugging tool is still careful thought, coupled with judiciously placed print statements.

text: Programs must be written for people to read, and only incidentally for machines to execute.
author: Harold Abelson and Gerald Jay Sussman
source: Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs (1985)

text: Adding manpower to a late software project makes it later.
author: Frederick P. Brooks Jr.

text: Plan to throw one away; you will, anyhow.
author: Frederick P. Brooks Jr.

text: A complex system that works is invariably found to have evolved from a simple system that worked.
author: John Gall

text: The purpose of a system is what it does.
author: Stafford Beer

text: It is a capital mistake to theorize before one has data.
author: Arthur Conan Doyle

text: When you can measure what you are speaking about, and express it in numbers, you know something about it.
author: Lord Kelvin
source: Lecture on Electrical Units of Measurement (1883)

text: The first principle is that you must not fool yourself, and you are the easiest person to fool.
author: Richard Feynman
source: Cargo Cult Science, Caltech commencement address (1974)

text: For a successful technology, reality must take precedence over public relations, for nature cannot be fooled.
author: Richard Feynman

text: What I cannot create, I do not understand.
author: Richard Feynman

text: All models are wrong but some are useful.
author: George E. P. Box
source: Robustness in the Strategy of Scientific Model Building (1979)

text: A map is not the territory it represents.
author: Alfred Korzybski

text: Talk is cheap. Show me the code.
author: Linus Torvalds

author: Linus Torvalds

text: Given enough eyeballs, all bugs are shallow.
author: Eric S. Raymond

text: Fancy algorithms are slow when n is small, and n is usually small.
author: Rob Pike

text: Data dominates. If you've chosen the right data structures and organized things well, the algorithms will almost always be self-evident.
author: Rob Pike

text: Clear is better than clever.
author: Rob Pike

text: A little copying is better than a little dependency.
author: Rob Pike

text: Errors are values.
author: Rob Pike

text: Make each program do one thing well.
author: Doug McIlroy

text: When in doubt, use brute force.
author: Ken Thompson

text: It is easier to write an incorrect program than understand a correct one.
author: Alan J. Perlis

text: Simplicity does not precede complexity, but follows it.

text: Fools ignore complexity. Pragmatists suffer it. Some can avoid it. Geniuses remove it.
author: Alan J. Perlis

text: Be conservative in what you do, be liberal in what you accept from others.
author: Jon Postel

text: To me, legacy code is simply code without tests.
author: Michael Feathers

text: Optimism is an occupational hazard of programming: feedback is the treatment.

text: Make it work, make it right, make it fast.
author: Kent Beck

text: APIs should be easy to use and hard to misuse.

source: How to Design a Good API and Why it Matters (2006)

text: Make illegal states unrepresentable.
author: Yaron Minsky

author: Douglas Hofstadter

text: The key to performance is elegance, not battalions of special cases.
author: Jon Bentley and Doug McIlroy

text: There are only two hard things in Computer Science: cache invalidation and naming things.
author: Phil Karlton

text: We can only see a short distance ahead, but we can see plenty there that needs to be done.
author: Alan Turing
